# `m.futures.snapshots`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Snapshots of futures contracts: the latest trade, quote, minute bar, and session.

```python
m.futures.snapshots(symbols, *, product_code=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol`; `mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND` also keys by `LastQuoteLastUpdated` and `LastTradeLastUpdated` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Contract tickers, a contracts table, or `dm.ALL`. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `product_code` | Only contracts of this product (`"ES"`) or these (`["ES", "NQ"]`); None for every product. A table of codes, in a `ProductCode` column, reads each code as if passed alone; a live one is followed by `fetch()` and re-read by each `poll()` cycle. |  |
| `sort` | Such as `"ticker"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | Needs `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Such as `{"ticker_gte": "ES"}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Futures Contracts Snapshot (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Futures Basic | Not included |
| Futures Starter | 10-minute delayed |
| Futures Developer | 10-minute delayed |
| Futures Advanced | Real-time |
| Futures Business CME | Real-time |
| Futures Business CBOT | Real-time |
| Futures Business NYMEX | Real-time |
| Futures Business COMEX | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `details.ticker`. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `DetailsProductCode` | String | The identifier for the contract's product. | REST |
| `DetailsSettlementDate` | String | The day that this contract is settled. | REST |
| `LastMinuteOpen` | double | The opening price at the start of the minute bar. | REST |
| `LastMinuteHigh` | double | The highest price reached in the minute bar. | REST |
| `LastMinuteLow` | double | The lowest price reached in the minute bar. | REST |
| `LastMinuteClose` | double | The price at the end of the minute bar. | REST |
| `LastMinuteVolume` | long | The number of contracts traded in the minute bar. | REST |
| `LastMinuteLastUpdated` | Instant | The timestamp indicating the most recent update to the minute bar. | REST |
| `LastMinuteTimeframe` | String | The timeliness of the data as determined by your subscription. One of REAL-TIME or DELAYED. | REST |
| `LastQuoteBid` | double | The highest price a buyer is willing to pay. | REST |
| `LastQuoteBidSize` | long | The number of contracts available at the bid price. | REST |
| `LastQuoteAsk` | double | The lowest price a seller is willing to accept. | REST |
| `LastQuoteAskSize` | long | The number of contracts available at the ask price. | REST |
| `LastQuoteBidTimestamp` | Instant | The time when the best bid price was last updated. | REST |
| `LastQuoteAskTimestamp` | Instant | The time when the best ask price was last updated. | REST |
| `LastQuoteLastUpdated` | Instant | The time when the quote was generated at the exchange to nanosecond precision. | REST |
| `LastQuoteTimeframe` | String | The timeliness of the data as determined by your subscription. One of REAL-TIME or DELAYED. | REST |
| `LastTradePrice` | double | The trade price is quoted per unit of the underlying asset, with the total contract value determined by multiplying by the contract’s specific multiplier. | REST |
| `LastTradeSize` | long | The total number of contracts exchanged between buyers and sellers on a given trade. | REST |
| `LastTradeLastUpdated` | Instant | The time when the trade was generated at the exchange to nanosecond precision. | REST |
| `LastTradeTimeframe` | String | The timeliness of the data as determined by your subscription. One of REAL-TIME or DELAYED. | REST |
| `SessionOpen` | double | The opening price at the start of the session. | REST |
| `SessionHigh` | double | The highest price reached in the session. | REST |
| `SessionLow` | double | The lowest price reached in the session. | REST |
| `SessionClose` | double | The price at the end of the session. | REST |
| `SessionVolume` | long | The number of contracts traded in the session. | REST |
| `SessionChange` | double | The change in price during this session. | REST |
| `SessionChangePercent` | double | The percentage change in price during this session. | REST |
| `SessionPreviousSettlement` | double | The settlement price of the previous session. | REST |
| `SessionSettlementPrice` | double | The final settlement price at the end of the session. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
